description: We are a two-person team (Irfan Khattak and Mohammad Abdullah) who built the CLPS Lunar South Pole Horizon Browser a standalone, high-fidelity simulation and coordinate analysis engine. Using Python and ML, it bypasses legacy APIs to calculate orbital kinematics, thermodynamics, and 3D terrain navigation locally. We are not accepting additional members, as our architecture, physics engine, and UI are fully developed and ready for submission.
summary:
Lunar Horizon Analytics (CLPS Lunar South Pole Horizon Browser) is an interactive, physics-driven mission planning and 3D telemetry platform built for NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) and Artemis III programs. Missions to the Lunar South Pole face extreme operational hazards: low-angle sunlight cast across rugged crater rims creates prolonged shadows, rapid thermal drops, and frequent Direct-to-Earth communication blackouts. Existing ephemeris and mapping tools require complex, multi-interface workflows that slow down rapid scenario comparison when launch dates or landing targets shift.

Built in Python with Streamlit, NumPy, and Plotly, our application translates lunar ephemeris mechanics and 360-degree crater elevation geometry into an intuitive, zero-latency Mission Control dashboard. Users can evaluate curated NASA Artemis III and CLPS candidate sites or drag and drop custom JSON/CSV coordinates to simulate hourly Sun and Earth vectors, battery charge/drain cycles, stateful hardware temperatures, autonomous A* rover pathfinding, and Lunar Gateway NRHO relay handshakes. An integrated 365-day Launch Window Optimizer, deterministic AI Mission Copilot, and one-click Flight Readiness PDF generator make complex lunar flight dynamics accessible to mission planners, educators, and students alike.
details:
Overview & Challenge Alignment

Lunar Horizon Analytics directly addresses the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge by bridging the gap between raw celestial ephemeris data and agile mission decision-making. Rather than forcing engineers and educators to cross-reference multiple complex tools, our platform unifies solar illumination, thermal survival, terrain traversability, and deep-space communications into a single interactive workspace.

Deployed Project Link : https://clps-lunar-south-pole-horizon-browser-azz8mvfmt6j4x9cvgetuko.streamlit.app/

Dual-Scale System Architecture

  1. Surface Topography (Micro View):
    • 3D Crater & Vector Raycasting: Models an airless lunar horizon by raycasting hourly Sun and Earth elevation/azimuth angles against a 360-degree crater rim elevation profile. Color-coded 3D vectors immediately alert planners when local topography blocks solar arrays (yellow-to-red transition) or severs Earth line-of-sight.
    • Stateful Lunar Thermodynamics: Simulates continuous hourly core temperature fluctuations (°C/hr) across sun-lit and permanently shadowed intervals, triggering automated freeze and overheat warnings.
    • Autonomous Rover Pathfinding: Computes a 3D A* navigation mesh across local crater terrain, evaluating slope gradients and dynamic shadow traps to automatically scrub routes exceeding a 25-degree tip-over limit.
    • Earth–Moon–Sun Kinematics: Visualizes the Moon’s 5.14° orbital inclination and umbra shadow cones in 3D space to identify lunar eclipse blackouts.
    • Lunar Gateway NRHO Relay: Models a 6.5-day Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) relay link that automatically establishes a backup telemetry bounce whenever crater walls obstruct Direct-to-Earth communications.
    • Custom Target Ingestion: Drag-and-drop JSON/CSV uploader for testing custom coordinates (such as Mons Mouton, Shackleton Connecting Ridge, Malapert A, and Haworth).
    • 365-Day Launch Window Optimizer: Brute-forces a full year of orbital mechanics to rank the top three backup launch windows when hardware or schedule delays force a scrub.
    • AI Mission Copilot & Export Suite: Provides a natural-language telemetry assistant and built-in Mission Primers for students/educators, alongside raw hourly CSV exports and automated Executive Briefing PDFs for flight planners.
